names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Θεόδωρος ο Μάρτυρας και οι συν αυτώ Φιλίππα, Διόσκορος, Σωκράτης και Διονύσιος», with the rank word left off; the life page heads him «Αγιος Διονύσιος».

Read out of the Охридски пролог's entry for 21. април ст. ст., „два војника, Сократа и Дионисија“ — **out of the entry's body and not out of its heading**, which names Theodore alone. The entry prints the name in the accusative there and nowhere in the nominative, so the form stored is that accusative read back into the nominative: a reading of the source's own word and not a transliteration, and flagged as a reading in the batch's commit message. The rank or kinship word beside it is left off, and the companionship clause this corpus keeps in the English display name is not part of the source's name.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Θεόδωρος ο Μάρτυρας και οι συν αυτώ Φιλίππα, Διόσκορος, Σωκράτης και Διονύσιος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page gives the company no years of its own: it sets Theodore and Dioscorus in the reign of the emperor Antoninus, which it dates 138 to 161 in one sentence and 138 to 160 in the next, and it names a governor Theodotus, so no `dates` were taken. Five people are named and enumerated on the page — Theodore, his mother Philippa, Dioscorus, and the two soldiers Socrates and Dionysius — and this corpus makes one folder for each. Theodore already had one: the corpus keeps him as theodore-of-perga, off the Romanian calendar's 21 aprilie, where doxologia.ro prints no life for him at all, so his Greek row is an upgrade on that folder and not a sixth arrival here. The corpus's four unnamed Martyrs of Perge, kept on 31 August, are a different entry and are not these. The page prints no hymn for the company.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 04.05.2026 (21. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Теодор.“

attestations.note: The Prologue's heading for the day names Theodore alone, „Св. муч. Теодор.“, and the entry's own first words are „И други с њим.“ — and others with him. The body then names the rest: the pagan priest Диоскор, who was condemned and burned, the two soldiers Сократ and Дионисије, run through with a spear, and Филипа, Theodore's mother, beheaded with the sword. So this row rests on the entry's enumeration of the company and not on the heading, which does not name him; the quoted line is the heading whole, as BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §4 requires.
